Earlier GPU/performance figures below retain their original revision labels. The latest pre-rebase heads were `6fff3b3f9` (#57523) and `74c82524e` (#64794).

## Overview

Let DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono decode on gfx950 read and write the 528 B MXFP8 KV record and read the 288 B NVFP4 compressed record. This follow-up depends on [#57523](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57523), which provides the ordinary attention readers and writers.

This is a stacked follow-up, not a replacement for #57523. Its prerequisite commits remain in the GitHub diff until that PR merges. The Mono-only delta is [the comparison against the parent branch](https://github.com/JohnQin-llm/vllm-amd/compare/rocm-dsv41-mxfp8-kv...dsv41-mono-kv-records).

## Claims

- Mono K1 writes 528 B MXFP8 window records, including quantized RoPE dimensions and per-32 scales.
- Mono K2 reads MXFP8 window records with MXFP8 or NVFP4 compressed records. It pads the NVFP4 compressed key list to complete 16-key tiles.
- Kernel build keys include the record format. The gfx942 NVFP4 exclusion remains.
- Keep V4.1 attention partials in FP32 until the chunk merge. V4 keeps BF16 partials.
- Mono supports the 528 B record. With aiter sparse MLA enabled, MXFP8 uses 528 B only when the installed aiter reader declares support; older aiter retains 584 B. NVFP4 aiter dispatch requires gfx950 and installed readers for both 528 B and 288 B records; older packages retain the ordinary fallback. The parent fixes for effective backend selection and consistent P/D layouts are preserved.

The parent uses legacy standalone Mono attention or an FFN-only fallback with the V4.1 record; this follow-up adds Mono attention support for both new formats.

## Validation

**Numerical regression fixed:** `74c82524e` fixes the TP8 MXFP8 `[8-8]` failure by removing the extra BF16 rounding of attention partials. The unchanged test passes twice (193.02 s and 160.06 s). At the failing position, output error falls from 3.25% to 1.74%; the first-layer bound remains 3%. Six additional real-LLM MXFP8/NVFP4 cases pass on committed source `74c82524e` (1050.43 s). Full-checkpoint results for this head are below.

Before the FP32 fix, production source `b567f3eed` with aiter `c910e55c7` was checked on MI355X (gfx950). At that point, the last amendment added only the NVFP4 TP8 CI selector; production files were identical to the tested `c8785dc28`. All pre-commit checks pass. The installed-reader gate passed with the new aiter package (27 checks) and the image's original package (28 checks). Real `LLM` NVFP4 backend-selection and numerical tests pass with aiter off/on at TP2 and on at TP8; MXFP8 model checks pass at TP4 and TP8 `[8-28]`. The new backend assertion fails on `79ba9c52e` before the fix and passes after it; numeric tolerances are unchanged.

Full-checkpoint DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash service results (1,319 questions each, 5-shot, max 256 output tokens, concurrency 64):

**Pre-rebase source `74c82524e`, aiter `5c7fc8d93` (runtime unchanged from `c910e55c7`):**

| Path (aiter + Mono enabled) | GSM8K accuracy | Unparseable | Eval time | Prefix hits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP8 NVFP4 | 90.67% | 1 | 28.2 s | 5376 |
| TP4 MXFP8 | 90.30% | 1 | 33.0 s | 5376 |
| TP2 NVFP4 | 90.75% | 0 | 44.3 s | 5376 |

Each configuration passed cold/hot prefix answers and mixed prefill/decode on every rank. Actual layer state reports aiter enabled, 528 B window records, and the expected 288 B or 528 B compressed records. Mono execution epochs advanced. These source-overlay checks are not a full package rebuild or a controlled end-to-end speed comparison.

An extra TP2 NVFP4 run with `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` also completed: 89.23% on 1,319 questions, 1 unparseable, 41.8 s, with prefix/mixed checks passing. This optional lossy-communication configuration is reported separately from the default results above.

<details>
<summary>Pre-FP32 service reference (`b567f3eed`)</summary>

| Path (aiter + Mono enabled) | GSM8K accuracy | Unparseable | Eval time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP2 NVFP4, run 1 | 89.46% | 0 | 42.4 s |
| TP2 NVFP4, run 2 | 90.60% | 1 | 40.4 s |
| TP4 MXFP8 | 90.90% | 0 | 34.8 s |
| TP8 NVFP4 | 91.05% | 0 | 27.8 s |

Every listed configuration also passed a cold/hot prefix-cache answer check (5,376 cache-hit tokens) and four streaming decodes overlapping four long prefills. Worker metadata observed mixed prefill/decode on every rank; layer state confirms aiter enabled and 528 B window records, with 288 B NVFP4 or 528 B MXFP8 compressed records. Mono's execution epoch advanced. These are serving and quality checks, not a controlled end-to-end speed comparison. Two TP2 runs with both aiter and Mono disabled scored 90.30% and 89.61%; greedy generation varies with batching.

</details>

All runs use Python source overlays on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505`, with the image's native ops, not a complete rebuild. Block 128, MXFP4 indexer/sparse logits, aiter MoE, CPU-offloaded Engram, default graph configuration, prefix caching, and `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` are used. gfx942 hardware qualification remains pending; the NVFP4 path is gfx950-only. The historical 300 s `sample_tokens` RPC timeout during inference on another node was not reproduced; its cause remains unknown. Cold startup includes FlyDSL compilation; TP8 engine initialization took 449.6 s. Startup used `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600`. Upstream GPU CI, gfx942 hardware and full package builds remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and regression evidence</summary>

With this branch and aiter `5c7fc8d93` overlaid on the pinned image:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py -k 'nvfp4_follows or v41_record_follows or stays_off_with_kv_connector'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py --tb=short
```

Before the routing fix, running the new `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model_nvfp4[2-True]` on `79ba9c52e` fails at `assert all(p["aiter"] == aiter for p in probe_on + probe_off)` after the two real LLM executions (1 failed). Relevant before/after output:

```text
# 79ba9c52e + the new regression test:
assert all(p["aiter"] == aiter for p in probe_on + probe_off)
E   assert False
1 failed in 194.67s
# Fixed production source, [2-False] and [2-True]:
2 passed in 254.52s
```

TP8 is selected explicitly in the 8-GPU CI step.

For a full service (set `TP=2`, `KV=nvfp4_ds_mla`; also tested `TP=4 KV=fp8` and `TP=8 KV=nvfp4_ds_mla`):

```bash
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name dsv41 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size "$TP" \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --block-size 128 --monokernel --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype "$KV"
# In a second shell, after /health succeeds:
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64 --save-results gsm8k.json
```

On `74c82524e`, all 80 Mono unit tests pass. The independent numerical fixture and 300 graph-replay checks pass for the three layouts in each controlled benchmark arm. The five-layer LLM numerics tests use random weights, eager execution and disabled prefix caching; full service checks above supply the separate scheduling/cache coverage.

</details>

### Performance

The FP32 correctness fix adds **1.5–3.5%** to V4.1 Mono K1+K2 time in this TP2 fixture. It removes an intermediate rounding; it is not a speed optimization. Legacy 584 B results range from −0.36% to +0.12%.

Microseconds per K1+K2 launch pair, including attention, seams and MoE. Fixed random weights, 128 window keys and 512 compressed keys; compressor/indexer work is excluded. Same MI355X pair and pinned image, `b567f3eed` → `74c82524e` → `b567f3eed`. Five repeats × 300 graph replays per arm, reporting the slower rank. Baseline medians pool ten samples. Maximum baseline drift is 0.73% (0.17% for V4.1 layouts).

| Rows | Ratio | Record layout | Before, median (range) | FP32 fix, median (range) | Time change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 1 | 584/584 | 122.78 (122.38–123.39) | 122.92 (122.85–123.07) | +0.12% |
| 48 | 2 | 584/584 | 461.04 (459.52–462.57) | 459.37 (459.06–459.73) | -0.36% |
| 6 | 1 | 528/528 | 122.59 (122.48–122.68) | 126.36 (126.28–126.45) | +3.07% |
| 48 | 2 | 528/528 | 459.26 (459.04–459.39) | 470.36 (470.26–470.45) | +2.42% |
| 6 | 1 | 528/288 | 123.53 (123.41–123.68) | 127.88 (127.84–127.98) | +3.52% |
| 48 | 2 | 528/288 | 461.48 (461.03–461.96) | 468.30 (468.23–468.44) | +1.48% |

Scratch reserves room for FP32 partials across record formats. The extra capacity per cached step width is at most 7.81 MiB at TP2, 3.75 MiB at TP4 and 1.88 MiB at TP8. If all 48 widths are cached, the extra per-runner capacity is 234.53/91.88/45.94 MiB at TP2/TP4/TP8.

This comparison runs all three layouts on both revisions. The same [reproducer](https://github.com/JohnQin-llm/vllm-amd/blob/dsv41-mono-benchmark/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mono_records.py) and commands below were used for this comparison. <details>
<summary>Earlier record-format comparison and reproduction commands</summary>

**µs per Mono K1+K2 launch pair**, including attention, seams and MoE. TP2 on two MI355X GPUs, random weights and fixed inputs from the numerical fixture; compressed caches/top-k are precomputed. Contexts are 2K–40K, 128 window keys and 512 compressed keys. This excludes the compressor/indexer and is not full-model throughput.

Order: parent `7da0be441` → compact head `ea023ae00` → parent, on the same GPU pair/image. Five repeats × 300 graph replays, reporting the slower rank. Baseline medians pool ten samples from both passes; PR medians use five. Baseline drift is at most 0.12%. These measurements predate the routing fixes, upstream rebase and FP32 partial fix. They are historical reference measurements.

| Rows | Compression ratio | Parent 584/584 | PR 584/584 | PR 528/528 | PR 528/288 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 1 | 122.56 | 122.79 (+0.19%) | 122.50 (-0.05%) | 123.52 (+0.78%) |
| 48 | 2 | 459.98 | 460.73 (+0.16%) | 459.43 (-0.12%) | 460.91 (+0.20%) |

<details>
<summary>Observed min–max (µs)</summary>

| Rows | Parent range | PR 584/584 range | PR 528/528 range | PR 528/288 range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | 122.47–122.76 | 122.72–122.85 | 122.32–122.57 | 123.31–123.59 |
| 48 | 459.73–460.35 | 460.65–461.08 | 459.29–459.77 | 460.77–461.02 |

</details>

[Reproducer](https://github.com/JohnQin-llm/vllm-amd/blob/dsv41-mono-benchmark/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mono_records.py) is on a companion branch to keep this diff small. With the selected Mono revision overlaid on the pinned image:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mono_records.py --records 528/528 --repeats 5 --iterations 300 --output mxfp8.json
# Also run 584/584 and 528/288; the parent supports 584/584 only.
```

</details>

## Details

The compaction merges duplicate writer stores, simplifies data loads/test setup, and removes repeated layout comments. Both record formats remain supported. The cache format is carried from the layer to the Mono runner and compile keys. The MXFP8 writer quantizes all 512 dimensions. The NVFP4 reader uses the gfx950 pair conversion and the per-16 e4m3 scales. Padding keeps each K2 key tile in one format.

BF16 rounding of each unnormalized attention partial added input error that the quantized MoE amplified. V4.1 retains FP32 partials until combination. On identical FFN input, the remaining Mono/reference FFN error is about 0.4%; the existing numerical thresholds are unchanged.

This follow-up includes a cached record-format capability check against the installed aiter reader and regression coverage for record selection. The aiter reader itself is tracked separately in [ROCm/aiter#7242](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/7242). User-facing format support and installed-reader requirements are documented under Hardware Supported Models.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex).

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Mono format support and installed-reader capability checks; aiter kernels remain in their separate PR.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** The gfx950 numerical, service/cache/mixed and model-eval checks pass; upstream GPU CI, gfx942 and full-build coverage remain open.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Focused diff and user documentation included; static check results recorded above.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Dependency, reproduction commands, validation limits are explicit.

</details>

+# DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono decode on ROCm
+
+On gfx950, `--monokernel` lets DeepSeek-V4.1 use Mono decode with its
+528-byte MXFP8 KV record. Enable it with `--monokernel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
+The record includes all 512 dimensions and 16 scale bytes per token.
+Without `--monokernel`, vLLM uses its ordinary attention path.
+
+With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1`, aiter uses MXFP8 only if
+its installed reader advertises the 528-byte record. Older aiter versions
+retain the 584-byte V4 record. On gfx950, aiter sparse MLA also supports NVFP4
+when its installed reader advertises both the 528-byte window and 288-byte
+compressed records. Otherwise NVFP4 uses the ordinary Triton attention path.
+
+With a KV connector, prefill and decode use the same 528-byte window record
+regardless of their Mono/aiter flags. Use the same model and cache dtype on
+both peers. Mono can read that record without the previous FFN-only fallback.
+
+The implementation also adds Mono reads of the 288-byte NVFP4 compressed
+record with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`. Its sliding-window cache stays
+in the 528-byte MXFP8 format. NVFP4 Mono support is limited to gfx950.
